key_idea: The visible skyline has slope +-1 everywhere it is above ground, so its length is sqrt(2) times the length of the union of the bases [x-y, x+y] clipped to [0, w].
sketch: This reduces to maintaining the length of a union of intervals under insertions and deletions. Read all queries offline, clip each interval to [0, w], compress endpoints, and use the classic cover-count segment tree (as in rectangle union area): each node stores how many intervals cover it fully and the covered length, with no push-down needed because every removal matches an earlier insertion. Toggle state is kept in a set keyed by the original peak (x, y), not the clipped interval. O(q log q). Pitfalls: 64-bit coordinates, clipping, and keying the toggle on the unclipped peak. Stress-tested against a brute force.
